Solvers Available to a Scoring Step

Source: R/solver.R
iwls_solvers.Rd

iwls() takes an argument solver, an object that selects the factorization with which each scoring step is solved. Three objects are available, built by solve_qr(), solve_svd() and solve_chol(); all three inherit from IwlsSolver. A character string is not accepted. Each constructor has the numerical tolerances of its factorization as arguments.

Value

No value. The topic describes the three objects, of classes SolveQR, SolveSVD and SolveChol, that solve_qr(), solve_svd() and solve_chol() return.

Details

The step solves \((X^\top W X + S)\,\delta = u\), where \(X\) is the design, \(W\) the diagonal matrix of the working weights (or, more generally, the per-observation curvature), \(S\) the Hessian of the penalty, and \(u\) the penalized score. The curvature is the matrix that the argument inner_information of statmod() selects (see information_objects). Let \(A = [\sqrt{W}X;\ \mathrm{chol}(S)]\), the design augmented by a factor of the penalty, so that \(A^\top A = X^\top W X + S\).

solve_qr()

Factors \(A\) by a QR decomposition, which does not form \(X^\top W X\), so the condition number of the system is not squared. Dense matrices use a QR with column pivoting, which drops a column that is numerically dependent on the others (the coefficient is reported as aliased) and records the rank; the argument tol is the tolerance of that decision. Sparse matrices use a sparse QR, which declines a rank-deficient system, and the step is then solved by the dense route. This is the default.

solve_svd()

Factors \(A\) by a singular value decomposition and applies the pseudo-inverse. A singular value below the cut tol (by default \(\max(\mathrm{dim}(A))\,\epsilon\,\sigma_{\max}\), with \(\epsilon\) the machine precision) is discarded, so a deficient system gives a minimum-norm step and a numerical rank, and no coordinate is reported as aliased because a discarded direction is a combination of columns. It is the dearest of the three and has no sparse counterpart.

solve_chol()

Factors the assembled information \(X^\top W X + S\) by a Cholesky decomposition, after flooring the eigenvalues of a matrix that is not positive definite at the relative level floor. The matrix is formed explicitly, so the condition number is squared; the design of a break-point term is bounded only to \(\epsilon^{-1/2}\), so the squaring can exhaust double precision.

solve_qr() and solve_svd() need a square root of the per-observation curvature and of the penalty. Where either does not exist (an observed curvature far from the optimum, a non-convex penalty), the step is solved from the assembled information, as solve_chol() does, and the eigenvalues of a matrix that is not positive definite are floored at the floor of the solver. For this reason the three constructors have the argument floor.

The tolerances and their defaults are:

ArgumentMeaningDefault
tol of solve_qr()pivoted QR rank tolerance1e-7
tol of solve_svd()relative cut of the singular valuesNULL, that is \(\max(\mathrm{dim}(A))\,\epsilon\)
floor of the threerelative floor of the eigenvalues1e-8

The test of the sparse QR, which compares the equilibrated diagonal of the triangular factor with \(\mathrm{ncol}(A)\,\epsilon\), is not an argument.

See also

solve_qr(), solve_svd() and solve_chol() for the constructors; iwls() for the function that takes the object; information_objects for the matrix that the solver factors.

Examples

solve_qr()
#> QR solver (tol 1e-07, floor 1e-08)
solve_svd(tol = 1e-12)
#> SVD solver (tol 1e-12, floor 1e-08)
solve_chol(floor = 1e-10)
#> Cholesky solver (floor 1e-10)

# The three reach the same fit on a design of full rank.
set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(120, -2, 2))
dd$y <- sin(1.4 * dd$x) + rnorm(120, sd = 0.3)
G <- distributions7::gaussian1_distrib()
f_qr <- statmod(y ~ s(x, bspline_smooth(k = 8)), G, dd,
                inner_optimizer = iwls(solver = solve_qr()),
                outer_criterion = NULL)
f_chol <- statmod(y ~ s(x, bspline_smooth(k = 8)), G, dd,
                  inner_optimizer = iwls(solver = solve_chol()),
                  outer_criterion = NULL)
max(abs(unlist(coef(f_qr)) - unlist(coef(f_chol))))
#> [1] 5.551115e-17
